text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT synth-canary-eu1 — 92% probe failures in 5m window (503 / connection resets). Rule: synth/prober/eu1 > 0.6 fail_rate. PagerDuty P1 auto-fired to @mike_oncall. probe_run_id=synth-eu1-20260315-09:12

mike_oncall: acked on PD and in channel, i'm taking it. pinging ash.

ash_sre: on it. grabbing logs + dashboards now. can anyone confirm scope? EU-only?

elena_prod: looks EU only from the quick heatmap. no user-facing errors reported in console or support slack yet.

sam_ops: adding runbook link: https://redwood/runbooks/synth-canary-failures — follow mitigation step 2 (reduce fanout) if high error rate.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident INC-1765554321 created and assigned to mike_oncall. Escalation timer 5m -> jen_tl if unacknowledged.

ash_sre: quick check, tailing prober logs: lots of 503s with upstream msg "target-concurrency-limit" and intermittent TCP resets. looks upstream rate-limiting at edge.

mike_oncall: can we confirm if it's our prober change or target service flapping? any recent prober roll?

elena_prod: we pushed a canary prober config earlier with increased fanout (parallelism=12) at 09:05. might be correlated.

ash_sre: pulling the rollout history now. yep — config etag=cfg-abc123 applied 09:06 to synth-eu1. reverting to previous (parallelism=4) should reduce pressure.

sam_ops: I can pause canary fanout from the control plane. doing that now -> issuing API call:

```
# pause fanout
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood-inference/prober/eu1/pause?etag=cfg-abc123
```

ash_sre: also running a quick curl against target endpoint from eu-prober node to reproduce:

```
curl -i -sS https://target-eu.example/api/health -H "x-prober: synth-eu1" -m 5
# response shows 503 + header X-Rate-Limit-Reason: concurrency
```

mike_oncall: paused fanout (sam_ops). confirming pause applied?

sam_ops: pause accepted, fanout scaled from 12 -> 3 (approx).

ash_sre: re-running the synthetic run. requeued probes, initial results look better — failure rate down to ~8% in the last 2m.

elena_prod: no customer reports and traffic graphs show normal user traffic. looks like prober was the primary pressure source.

jen_tl: thanks team. if stable, we should roll back the canary config and follow up with a postmortem. please keep PD incident open until stable for 30m.

mike_oncall: agree. rolling back prober config to etag=cfg-xyz789 (previous).

ash_sre: rollback command applied:

```
# rollback prober config
redwoodctl prober apply --space eu1 --config-etag cfg-xyz789
```

ash_sre: monitors show stabilization. synth fail_rate ~1% over last 6m. no more 503s from prober.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident INC-1765554321 acknowledged by mike_oncall; escalations suppressed.

mike_oncall: filing incident ticket and short blameless summary. tag: synth-canary-eu1, trigger=prober-fanout-change.

elena_prod: customer impact assessment: none observed — synthetic-only, no production errors. severity: P1 automated but business impact = low. recommended: update runbook to warn about fanout increases and add preflight throttle check.

jen_tl: good note. assign action items: ash -> postmortem draft, sam -> add control-plane guardrail, elena -> update runbook. target 48h.

mike_oncall: closing channel for now, will keep PD incident open for 30m and then resolve if clean. thanks all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: NOTE: auto-note added to ticket INC-1765554321 — "root cause: prober fanout increase caused upstream concurrency limits; mitigation: paused fanout & rolled back config; status: stable"

ash_sre: quick follow-up: push a small guardrail so future prober fanout >8 requires manual approval. I'll open a PR.

sam_ops: also adding an alert to flag sudden fanout config changes in the future (audit + guardrail).

mike_oncall: last check at 09:50 — system stable. resolving on PD in 25m if no regressions.

elena_prod: thanks team. adding a note to customer comms channel in case any indirect anomalies show up.

jen_tl: well handled. postmortem when ready. :white_check_mark:
